questions.prompt: A response may be stored but must be validated before reuse. Which Cache-Control directive expresses that requirement?

choices.text: no-store permits storage but requires a validation on each subsequent reuse.
public prevents storage by every shared cache while enabling browser storage.
immutable forces all caches to contact the origin before every reuse.
no-cache requires validation before using the stored response.

questions.explanation: No-cache allows storage while requiring successful validation before reuse. No-store instead prohibits storing the response.

sources.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
sources.claim: HTTP caching distinguishes storage, freshness and validation; no-cache requires validation, no-store prohibits storage, and Vary affects reuse.

questions.prompt: A cache compares a stored response current age to its freshness lifetime. When is it fresh?

choices.text: Its current age is greater than its freshness lifetime.
It has an ETag, regardless of its current age and freshness lifetime.
Its freshness lifetime is greater than its current age.
It permits storage, regardless of its current age and freshness lifetime.

questions.explanation: Freshness is determined by lifetime versus current age. Validators and HTTPS do not by themselves make an expired response fresh.

questions.prompt: A cache has an ETag for a stored GET response. Which request header supports validation of that representation?

choices.text: If-Modified-Since carries the stored entity tag as its validator value.
If-None-Match carries the stored entity tag.
Cache-Control carries the entity tag in a max-age directive.
Vary carries the stored entity tag to match the server current version.

questions.explanation: If-None-Match tests the stored entity tag. The other headers serve different purposes and are not cache validators.

questions.prompt: An endpoint selects a representation using Accept-Language. What response field tells caches to account for that request header?

choices.text: Vary: Accept-Language identifies an additional matching dimension.
Content-Language alone adds the language request header to cache matching.
Cache-Control: public automatically partitions cache entries by all request headers.
ETag automatically partitions every stored representation by Accept-Language.

questions.explanation: Vary lists request fields that affect representation selection and reuse. Merely stating response language does not establish that cache matching rule.

questions.prompt: A personalized response must not be stored by shared caches but may be stored by the user private cache. Which unqualified directive matches?

choices.text: no-cache prevents shared-cache storage but permits immediate private reuse.
no-store prevents shared-cache storage but still permits private-cache storage.
max-age=0 prevents shared-cache storage while keeping browser entries fresh.
private restricts storage to private caches.

questions.explanation: Unqualified private prohibits shared-cache storage. No-store prohibits storage more generally; max-age controls freshness rather than cache ownership.

questions.prompt: A shared cache sees both `s-maxage=60` and `max-age=600`. Which freshness directive governs that shared cache?

choices.text: max-age overrides s-maxage because it applies to all cache implementations.
The cache adds both values to create a combined 660-second lifetime.
s-maxage overrides max-age for the shared cache.
The cache uses the larger lifetime because either directive can establish freshness.

questions.explanation: S-maxage specifies shared-cache freshness and overrides max-age there. The values are not added or chosen by maximum.

questions.prompt: A team chooses storage policies for API responses. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: public guarantees that each authenticated user receives a separately keyed cache entry.
no-store prohibits storing the response.
no-cache allows storage but requires validation before reuse.
private prevents unqualified shared-cache storage.
no-cache guarantees the response is never stored.

questions.explanation: a: Public permits shared caching; it does not automatically isolate representations by user identity. b: That directive targets storage itself. c: It is a reuse constraint rather than a storage ban. d: Private responses may still be stored privately. e: It is not equivalent to no-store.

questions.prompt: A cache determines freshness. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Freshness uses a lifetime and current age.
max-age supplies an explicit freshness lifetime.
A private browser cache must prefer s-maxage over max-age.
An ETag keeps the response fresh after its declared freshness lifetime expires.
HTTPS makes every cached response permanently reusable.

questions.explanation: a: The comparison determines whether the response remains fresh. b: It is an explicit freshness directive. c: S-maxage targets shared caches, not the private browser cache. d: Validators support checking a stale entry, not extending freshness on their own. e: Secure transport does not remove freshness rules.

questions.prompt: A stored response has validators. Which revalidation claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A 304 can update stored metadata without a full representation body.
Validation can allow a stored body to be reused.
A 304 always contains a complete replacement response body.
Content-Length is the standard entity-tag validator.
If-None-Match can send stored entity tags.

questions.explanation: a: A cache merges relevant 304 fields into the stored response. b: Successful validation confirms reuse is appropriate. c: 304 responses do not transfer the full representation body. d: ETag and If-None-Match provide the entity-tag mechanism. e: The validator supports conditional requests.

questions.prompt: A response includes Vary. Which matching rules hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Vary is irrelevant once a response has a long max-age.
Vary: * allows reuse for any request-header values.
Vary changes the browser origin of the stored response.
Listed request fields affect stored-response matching.
Vary can prevent reuse across language variants.

questions.explanation: a: Freshness does not waive representation matching. b: The wildcard prevents determining a suitable match for subsequent reuse. c: It changes matching criteria, not the response origin. d: A cache compares the nominated field values. e: Accept-Language can be included in the match criteria.
